chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, that Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, said:

"Verily, no one among the people possesses any truth or correctness except what they have taken from us, the Ahlul Bayt. And no one among the people judges with truth or justice except that the key of that judgment, its gate, its origin, and its way is Amirul Mu'mineen Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. So when matters become confused for them, the error is from their own side when they err, and the correctness is from the side of Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, when they are right."

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahlul Bayt - the People of the House, referring to the Prophet's household
key_terms.القضاء: Judgment - just legal and religious rulings
key_terms.مفتاح: Key - metaphor for Imam Ali as the essential means to access true judgment

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir say that Imam Ali is the key to all just judgment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) affirms the exclusive authority of the Ahlul Bayt as the source of all truth and correct judgment among the people, declaring that Imam Ali (AS) is the key, the gate, and the origin of just rulings. This teaching was directed at the Shia community to reinforce the foundational doctrine of Imamate and the indispensable role of divinely appointed guides in matters of religious and legal authority.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibnAbdillah, from Ahmed ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who reported that: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon him said:

"People (who have discarded us) have no truth, nor any propriety, except that which they have learnt from us Ahlul Bayt. None from them can judge truly or with justice, unless he has taken its guidance from Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, the key, the gate, the path blazer, the way. And when they are confused in any matter, the fault is theirs if they commit an error; and if they decide rightly, the credit goes to ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (as)."
